newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, livestock dealers said.
Prices were expected to be pressured by active hog marketings late last week and on Tuesday, which provided more than adequate inventories for packers, they said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen ranging from $57.50 to $58.00. Illinois top prices at plants were seen at $57.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs shipped to the plant could range $57.00 to $57.50.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Friday totaled 102,000 head, above the day's estimate for 95,000. Saturday's receipts totaled 14,000 compared with the estimate of 15,000. Monday's estimate for 110,000 head.
Active marketings supplied at least one major meat packer in the Midwest with enough hogs for Wednesday's slaughter by midday on Tuesday, a packer buyer said.

Soft pork demand also was expected to contribute to Wednesday's lower hog prices. Fresh retail pork were not well tested near midday, with hams, bellies and lean trimmings generally steady, USDA said in its carlot pork report. It reported 11.0 loads of pork and 6.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
